Done. Reflection summary:

What went wrong: My answer [0.4, 1967] vs gold [7.1, 82] was wrong on BOTH sub-questions in characteristic ways:
- Sub-answer 2 (absolute change in Series I redemptions): 1967 vs 82 ≈ 24x too big → I read a fiscal-year-to-date/cumulative redemptions column (or grabbed the total-redemptions row) instead of the single March monthly Series I cell.
- Sub-answer 1 (share change in percentage points): 0.4 vs 7.1 ≈ 18x too small → I mis-identified the Series I row or used the wrong (too-large) total-redemptions denominator.

What's generalizable and saved:
1. Skill patch — added a new section "SHARE of total redemptions accounted for by ONE series (e.g. Series I/EE) in a MONTH" to the officeqa-treasury-bulletin skill. It documents the formula (share = seriesX_monthly_red / all_series_monthly_red × 100, change = signed difference; abs change = |Series I diff|), the monthly-vs-cumulative-column trap, the modern-series (Series I intro Sep 1998, EE) row-identification trap, units, output order, and the two diagnostic fingerprints (24x overshoot = cumulative/total error; 18x undershoot = wrong row/denominator).
2. Memory — added a compact durable note capturing the single-month-cell rule and the diagnostics, since memory was full I folded it into the existing savings-bond entry.

This was genuinely new: the skill previously covered redemption RATE and sales-vs-redemptions distinctions, but not the "share of total monthly redemptions by series" pattern, the cumulative-column trap, or the modern Series I/EE identification trap.
